Here’s what I can tell you from memory about the 2014–15 Missouri State Lady Bears women’s basketball team:

- Program/context
  - School: Missouri State University (Springfield, Missouri)
  - Conference: Missouri Valley Conference (MVC)
  - Home court: JQH Arena
  - Head coach: Kellie Harper (second season at Missouri State in 2014–15)
  - Brand: “Lady Bears” is the longtime moniker for the women’s program

- Season arc (high level)
  - This season marked an uptick under Kellie Harper after a rebuilding first year. The team found its footing in MVC play and, as I recall, earned a postseason berth (WNIT), not the NCAA Tournament.
  - They were competitive in the Valley, finishing in the upper tier of the league and making a run at the MVC Tournament, but Wichita State was the dominant MVC program at that time and stood in the way of an NCAA automatic bid.

- Likely record/finish (from memory, not guaranteed exact)

  - MVC record was strong (something like 12–6 or 13–5), placing them near the top of the standings.
  - Postseason: WNIT appearance.

- Notable players and honors (from memory)
  - Kenzie Williams (G): Breakout performer and All-MVC caliber guard this season.
  - Tyonna Snow (G): Dynamic two-way guard known for defense, toughness, and getting to the rim; an All-Defensive Team-level player in the Valley around this time.
  - Liza Fruendt (G, freshman in 2014–15): Impact freshman scorer; earned MVC All-Freshman Team honors (and may have been in the Freshman of the Year conversation).
  - Hillary Chvatal (F): Frontcourt contributor and veteran presence.
  - Depth around the perimeter was a strength; scoring balance improved as the year went on.

- Coaching staff (from memory)
  - Assistants included Jon Harper, Jennifer Sullivan, and program legend Jackie Stiles.

- Style/identity
  - Guard-driven team that defended, rebounded, and played with pace when possible.
  - Emphasis on toughness and half-court defense under Harper, with the offense leaning on attacking guards.

- Legacy/trajectory
  - 2014–15 is often viewed as a solid step that set the stage for bigger things. Under Harper, Missouri State broke back through to the NCAA Tournament the following season (2015–16) and later enjoyed even deeper March runs under Amaka Agugua-Hamilton.
  - The players from this roster—especially Williams, Snow, and Fruendt—were foundational in reestablishing the Lady Bears as MVC contenders.
